stem: Suspicion is arguably a natural self-protective instinct essential to the survival of individuals and societies: a human being or community that is totally ____ is inviting trouble.
In general memoirs focus sharply on particular, and particularly memorable, events rather than on the entire life. This (i)____ structure inevitably emphasizes drama at the expense of (ii)____.

Human brains are amazing organs but they are not perfect. Cognitive biases, as we know, sometimes produce errors. Yet the term "error" could be (i)____ in that it suggests that there might be (ii)____ way in which cognition should work. Such a binary opposition is (iii)____.
Although the writer meant for the book to serve as a kind of tribute to motherhood, the approach here is hardly a ____ affair.

Although biologists know that thousands of species of microbes and invertebrates inhabit one square meter of temperate grassland soil, the identities of those creatures and their contributions to sustaining the biosphere remain ____.
Although a dedicated reader of the book can ____ a brief of chronology of Chappell’s life, the book is nevertheless not a real biography of Chapelle.
Physicians today increasingly rely on endoscopic surgery, ____ large scalpels and clamps in favor of endoscopy’s cameras and flexible tools that can snake into the body through tiny holes.
